questions.question:
**Direction- In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Hyperbole
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The best option that expresses the meaning of the given word** "Hyperbole"** is **option 2, "Overstatement."**
 
• The word** "Hyperbole" **refers to **an exaggerated statement or claim that is not meant to be taken literally, usually used for emphasis or effect**.
 
 
• For example, "He is so hungry that he could eat a horse" is a hyperbole because it exaggerates the degree of hunger to make a point.
 
 
 
• **Overstatement **refers to **the act of exaggerating something beyond its actual significance or importance**. It is a type of **hyperbole **that is used to emphasize a point or to make something appear more impressive or dramatic.
 
 
• Example of overstatement: "I've been waiting for ages." - In this sentence, the speaker is using overstatement to exaggerate the amount of time they've been waiting. They may not have actually been waiting for a very long time, but they want to emphasize their impatience.
 
 
 
• **Option 1, "Spoliation," **refers to the act of plundering or looting, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "The invaders engaged in **spoliation **of the city's treasures" means that the invaders looted the city's treasures.
 
 
 
• **Option 3, "Simplification,"** refers to the process of making something simpler or easier to understand, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "She **simplified **the instructions for the children to follow" means that she made the instructions easier to understand for the children.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "Injury," **refers to physical harm or damage caused to a person or object, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "He suffered a severe **injury **to his leg in the accident" means that he suffered physical harm to his leg.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 2, "Overstatement," **which accurately expresses the meaning of **"Hyperbole."**

questions.question: Which among the following have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Only women.**

__**EXPLANATION:**__

__
 
• Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes XX while men have a mismatched pair in which one is a normal-sized X and the other a short one Y which is XY.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__

 
• Chromosomes are structures found in the center (nucleus) of cells that carry long pieces of DNA. DNA is the material that holds genes. It is the building block of the human body.
 
• Chromosomes also contain proteins that help DNA exist in the proper form.
 
• Chromosomes come in pairs.
 
• Normally, each cell in the human body has 23 pairs of chromosomes (46 total chromosomes).
 
• Half comes from the mother, the other half comes from the father.
 
• Two of the chromosomes (the X and the Y chromosome) determine your sex as male or female when you are born. They are called sex chromosomes:
 
• Females have 2 X chromosomes.
 
• Males have 1 X and 1 Y chromosome.
 
• The mother gives an X chromosome to the child. The father may contribute an X or a Y. The chromosome from the father determines if the baby is born male or female.
 
• A human being has 23 pairs of chromosomes in which one pair of X and Y chromosomes determine the sex of the human being.
 
• If there is one X chromosome from the mother and one X chromosome from the father, then two X chromosomes (XX) make a girl whereas the X chromosome from the mother and Y chromosome from the father then these chromosomes (XY) make a boy.
 
• The remaining chromosomes are called autosomal chromosomes.
 
• They are known as chromosome pairs 1 through 22.
